PC:
Obtain pertinent history.
Progressive paresthesias, numbness and weakness for the past week.
Preceded by diarrheal infection 3-4 weeks prior.
Inquired about bulbar symptoms (e.g. difficulty swallowing, soft voice, drooling, slurred speech)
Inquired about respiratory symptoms (e.g. dyspnea, orthopnea)
Inquired about dysautonomic symptoms (e.g. constipation, urinary retention, orthostatic hypotension)

Perform pertinent neurological exam.
Assess mental status.
Assess cranial nerves.
Assess limb strength.
Assess reflexes.
Assess sensation.
Assess high yield neuromuscular exam findings (if not previously done in #1) – particularly, neck flexion and/or breath counting.
Order diagnostic tests (or review from outside hospital ED records).
MK: Recognize that patient has decline in mental status & vitals/respiratory status despite NIV.
SBP: Call respiratory therapist (RT) & ask them to check NIF/FVC & ABG.
Call anesthesia for STAT intubation & transfer to ICU.
